title: The Ansar’s Worry • Hind and Abu Quhafah • The Days After the Victory • In Crowds • Final Word

blocks.1: Makkah was conquered. The Ansar began to whisper among themselves; the man has felt the pull of his own city, affection for his relatives has stirred. Now perhaps he will stay right here. Through revelation the Prophet {{1}} came to know. He called the Ansar and asked, have you said such a thing? They admitted it. He said,
blocks.3: Never. I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger. I migrated to Allah and to you. My living is with your living, my dying with your dying.{{1}}
blocks.4: The Ansar came forward weeping. They said, by Allah, what we said was only out of attachment to Allah and His Messenger, out of fear of losing him. The Prophet {{1}} said, Allah and His Messenger affirm you as truthful, they accept your excuse. On the day the city of his birth, where the Ka‘bah is, came into his hands, he did not forget who had given him shelter. It is easy to make the companions of the days of hardship strangers in the days of ease; he did not do that. When a new opportunity comes today, do I not push the old faithful people behind for it tomorrow?
blocks.6: Among those who accepted Islam was Hind bint ‘Utbah (RA); who at Uhud had taken Hamzah’s (RA) liver into her mouth. Coming to the Prophet {{1}} she said,
blocks.8: O Messenger of Allah, there was no household on the face of the earth whose humiliation was dearer to me than the humiliation of the people of your household. And today there is no household on the face of the earth whose honour is dearer to me than the honour of the people of your household. The Prophet {{1}} said, by the One in whose hand is my soul, it will increase further.{{2}}
blocks.9: In one day a heart turned upside down; the household whose humiliation was dearest, the honour of that very household became dearest. Forgiveness does not merely let the enemy go; sometimes it turns the enemy into a friend.
blocks.11: Abu Bakr (RA) brought his old, sightless father Abu Quhafah, leading him by the hand, to the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} said, you should have left the old man at home; I would have gone to him.{{3}}
blocks.12: The Prophet {{1}} seated him in front, stroked his chest and gave him the call to Islam, and Abu Quhafah (RA) accepted Islam. His head and beard were completely white. The Prophet {{2}} said, dye this white hair with something.{{3}}
blocks.13: The busiest day of the victory. Yet he felt bad that a blind old man had had to walk to come. Respect for age, respect for a companion’s father; in the excuse of busyness these were not lost.
blocks.15: The next day the Prophet {{1}} stood to give a sermon. Abu Shurayh al-‘Adawi (RA) used to say later, my two ears heard, my heart remembered, my two eyes saw, when he said this. He praised Allah, then said,
blocks.17: Allah made Makkah sacred, people did not. For one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, it is not lawful to shed blood here, nor to cut down a tree. If anyone makes the fighting of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ an excuse, tell him, Allah had permitted His Messenger, He did not permit you. I was permitted for one hour of the day. Today its sanctity is again as it was yesterday. Let the one present convey it to the one absent.{{1}}
blocks.19: In Makkah there was permission for war for one hour. As soon as the hour ended, the announcement: today again sacred as before. The hand that had the sword returned it. On the very first day after the victory the limit was announced from the victor’s mouth. As much as the power, that much is the limit; because power is never one’s own. He announced another thing too,
blocks.21: After today, until the Day of Resurrection, no Qurayshi will be bound and killed.{{1}}
blocks.23: The leaders of the enemies were then unarmed before him. The chance to bind and kill was in hand. That door of chance he shut with his own mouth. Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) asked, O Messenger of Allah, where will you stay tomorrow? His own city, his own home. The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.27: Whatever houses there were, after the hijrah they had gone into ‘Aqil’s hands. The Prophet {{1}} did not rush after that house. The tent was pitched at Hajun. The house he had left for Allah, even on the day of victory the thought of taking it back did not occupy him. We often rush, when we get the chance, to take back first of all what we have left behind. When power and opportunity come into hand, it is one’s own lost things that come to mind first. He remembered first of all: this is the day of the city’s sanctity. Makkah became a city of the Muslims. So after the conquest the command to migrate from Makkah no longer remained. The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.29: After the conquest of Makkah there is no hijrah; there is jihad and intention. And when you are called to set out, set out.{{1}}
blocks.31: When the place changes the name of the deed changes. In place of hijrah came jihad and intention. The intention which, when it is there, does not require leaving the house, yet when the call comes does not hesitate to leave the house. On the morning of the victory Umm Hani (RA) went and saw the Prophet {{1}} bathing, his daughter Fatimah (RA) holding up a curtain. After the bath the Prophet {{2}}, wrapped in a single cloth, prayed eight rak‘ahs. Umm Hani says, it was the time of Duha.{{3}}
blocks.32: On the morning of the victory, no festival; eight rak‘ahs of prayer. After conquering a city the first deed was sujud. After some great success we first give the news, take pictures, celebrate. He first stood before Allah. He stayed nineteen days in Makkah. He prayed two rak‘ahs at a time. His own birthplace, yet in the city he had left by hijrah, the prayer of a traveller.{{1}}
blocks.34: After the conquest of Makkah the tribes of Arabia seemed to break out of waiting. All along they had been watching who would win in the fight between Quraysh and Muhammad. Now they began to come in crowds. The Qur’an had told of this day beforehand in this way,
blocks.36: When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in crowds, then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness. Surely He is the Most Forgiving.{{1}}
blocks.37: The command of the day of victory is not festival, but tasbih and istighfar. And Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) saw one more thing in this surah; the work has come to completion, the time of farewell too is near.{{1}}
blocks.38: When a big work is finished people usually count their own achievement. The Qur’an taught the opposite reckoning; praise is Allah’s, and asking forgiveness for oneself.
blocks.40: From the days of the conquest of Makkah a few pictures stay before the eye. The water vessel held up beside the spring of Kadid. The cousin who wanted to set out with his son’s hand to die, and the Prophet’s slap on his chest, you are the one who drove me out. The ten thousand fires of Marr al-Zahran, and the declaring of Abu Sufyan’s house a refuge. Entering with a bowed head, chin on the howdah, reciting Surah al-Fath. At the door of the Ka‘bah, all the claims of blood of Jahiliyyah beneath the feet. The Ansar’s weeping, and in answer, my living and dying are with you. Hind’s heart turned upside down. For blind Abu Quhafah, I would have gone myself. Abu Sufyan’s running about in Madinah and ‘Ali’s small answer, the decision has been made. Inside the Ka‘bah the pictures drawn in the name of Ibrahim (AS), without removing which he did not set foot in the house. Withholding his hand three times for Ibn Abi Sarh, and then saying, deceit by a hint is not for me. For Safwan his own turban, and saying, you are given four months. The next day’s sermon: Makkah is sacred, today again as before. Instead of rushing in search of the house that had gone into ‘Aqil’s hands, a tent at Hajun. On the morning of the victory, eight rak‘ahs of prayer. When power comes into hand, people change. Those at whose hands I suffered year after year, when they come into my fist, what do I do; the test is exactly there. So take away one deed from today’s dars.
blocks.42: Even with twenty years’ enemies in his fist, the Prophet {{1}} did not take revenge; on the day of victory he entered Makkah with a bowed head. Today I will ask myself a question: those from whom I have suffered, if they come into my fist, what will I do? Whatever chance of revenge I have in hand today, I will let it go; I will not keep this door of forgiveness shut from today.

The incident of Umm Hani’s protection was told in Dars 19; as for the eight rak‘ahs being two by two as a prayer of thanks for victory, there is explanation among the scholars; some called it the Duha prayer.

quiz.q: Thinking what, did the Ansar fall into worry?
o: They would get less spoils
Quraysh would fight again
The Prophet ﷺ would stay in Makkah
Their leadership would be taken away from now on
quiz.e: That out of the pull of the city and affection for relatives he would stay.

quiz.q: ‘My living and dying are with you’; what does this express?
o: Not forgetting the companions of hardship in days of ease
Aversion to Makkah
Frightening the Ansar
A temporary promise as a political strategy of Madinah
quiz.e: He did not leave those who had given shelter.

quiz.q: Hearing the Ansar’s excuse, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: Allah and His Messenger affirm you as truthful
You thought wrongly, repent
Never say this again
Your share of spoils will be reduced for your suspicion
quiz.e: ‘They affirm you as truthful, accept your excuse.’

quiz.q: A good opportunity has come in a new job; what do I do with the companions of old hard times?
o: Slowly reduce the relationship
Give my mind only to the new circle
Not forget them
Keep contact with them only when needed, not at other times
quiz.e: ‘My living and dying are with you.’

quiz.q: In a day of danger someone wept for me, and out of a wrong fear also spoke harsh words; what does the incident of the Ansar teach?
o: Cutting off the relationship over harsh words
Mocking his fear
Accepting a sincere excuse
Arranging severe punishment without hearing the excuse, so that a lesson is learned
quiz.e: ‘He accepts your excuse.’

quiz.q: Whispering is going on within the team about someone’s mistake; in the incident of the Ansar what did the Prophet ﷺ do?
o: Calling them directly, talking and settling it
Pretending not to hear
Punishing the whisperers
Arranging for others to keep watch on them
quiz.e: He called and asked, have you said this?

quiz.q: Hind bint ‘Utbah (RA) said whose household’s honour was dearest to her?
o: Abu Sufyan’s household
‘Utbah’s family
Quraysh’s biggest tribe
The Prophet’s ﷺ household
quiz.e: Today the honour of your household is the dearest.

quiz.q: Abu Quhafah (RA) was whose father?
o: Abu Bakr’s (RA)
‘Umar’s (RA)
‘Uthman’s (RA)
Abu ‘Ubaydah’s (RA)
quiz.e: The father of Abu Bakr (RA).

quiz.q: Seeing Abu Quhafah’s white hair, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: Leave it just so
Dye it with something
Cut it short
Shave the head, today itself
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 2102.

quiz.q: From Hind’s change, which aspect of forgiveness becomes clear?
o: Forgiveness is an expression of weakness
Forgiveness makes even an enemy a friend
Forgiveness is due only to relatives
If you forgive, the enemy becomes bolder and strikes again
quiz.e: In one day a heart turned upside down.

quiz.q: ‘Leave the old man at home, I would have gone’; what is the lesson of this?
o: Rebuking Abu Bakr
The old are forbidden to come to gatherings
Respect for age even in busyness
A sick person should never be invited
quiz.e: Even on the busy day of the victory, the hardship of a blind old man made him feel bad.

quiz.q: Someone who was earlier hostile to me is now showing love; what did the Prophet ﷺ do with Hind?
o: Keeping her at a distance with suspicion
Bringing up old matters and taunting
Ignoring her love and silently moving away
Answering love with love
quiz.e: ‘By the One in whose hand is my soul, it will increase.’

quiz.q: A friend’s elderly father wants to take the trouble to come to meet me; according to this dars what should be done?
o: Going myself to meet him
Letting him come
Avoiding by citing busyness
Settling it by phone alone, no need to meet
quiz.e: ‘I would have gone to him.’

quiz.q: In the sermon narrated by Abu Shurayh (RA), what was the announcement about Makkah?
o: No Qurayshi will be bound and killed again
All claims of blood of Jahiliyyah beneath the feet
Today there is no blame or rebuke upon you
The permission to fight was for one hour, today it is again sacred
quiz.e: Bukhari 104.

quiz.q: What does ‘after the conquest there is no hijrah; there is jihad and intention’ teach?
o: When the place changes the name of the deed changes, the intention remains
The whispers of enemies are not hidden from the Prophet ﷺ
Eight rak‘ahs on the morning of the victory
Claims of blood of Jahiliyyah beneath the feet
quiz.e: Bukhari 2783.

quiz.q: On the morning of victory, not festival first but standing before Allah first; which incident matches this?
o: Drinking water in daytime at Kadid
The Prophet’s ﷺ tent being pitched at Hajun
Entering bowed with the chin on the camel’s howdah
Eight rak‘ahs of prayer in Umm Hani’s house
quiz.e: Bukhari 357.

quiz.q: What does Surah al-Nasr say to do after victory?
o: Festival and feasts
A victory procession
Tasbih and istighfar
Making a list of enemies and trying them
quiz.e: Glorifying with praise and seeking forgiveness.

quiz.q: What hint did Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) see in Surah al-Nasr?
o: Another big war is coming
The capital will move from Madinah
The rules of Hajj will soon change completely
The Prophet’s ﷺ farewell is near
quiz.e: The work complete, the farewell near.

quiz.q: A big project has ended successfully; according to the lesson of Surah al-Nasr what is the first deed?
o: Publicising one’s achievement
Praise of Allah and istighfar
Jumping into the next project
Making a list of colleagues’ mistakes and telling everyone
quiz.e: After victory, tasbih and istighfar.

quiz.q: Someone who hurt me a lot is dependent on me today; according to the practical resolve what will I do?
o: Use the opportunity
Let go of the chance of revenge
Have someone else take the revenge
Help him, but each time reminding him of old matters
quiz.e: Letting go of the chance of revenge in hand.
